description: GlobTraceX is an Earth-system trend investigation platform developed by Team Protichamp for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It helps users explore environmental changes using NASA Earth-observation data, visualize trends, analyze their magnitude and statistical significance, and compare geographic regions and environmental signals. By connecting scientific analysis with clear visualizations and traceable data sources, GlobTraceX aims to turn complex Earth data into understandable, evidence-based insights.
summary:
GlobTraceX is an interactive Earth-system trend investigation platform developed by Team Protichamp, Bangladesh, for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It helps users move beyond isolated environmental measurements to explore patterns, regional differences, and long-term changes across our planet.

Using daily temperature and relative humidity data from NASA POWER, GlobTraceX introduces a Hot & Humid Days indicator based on explicitly defined thresholds: maximum temperature of at least 32°C and relative humidity of at least 70%. Users can select regions, explore environmental patterns through maps and visualisations, and investigate trends over time.

By making Earth-observation-related data more accessible and interpretable, GlobTraceX aims to support students, researchers, and curious citizens in understanding environmental change through transparent, evidence-oriented exploration. Its central goal is simple: make complex planetary data easier to investigate, compare, and communicate.
details:
Project Overview

GlobTraceX is an interactive platform designed to help people investigate environmental change through regional exploration, data visualisation, and trend-focused analysis. Developed by Team Protichamp, Bangladesh, the project responds to the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 theme, “Be an Earth System Trend Detective!”, by making environmental data easier to explore and interpret.

How It Works

Users can select a geographic region and explore environmental indicators through an interactive investigation interface. The current implementation uses NASA POWER daily meteorological data, including maximum temperature (T2M_MAX) and relative humidity (RH2M).

To make these variables easier to interpret together, our team defined a Hot & Humid Days indicator. A day is flagged when maximum temperature is at least 32°C and relative humidity is at least 70%. These thresholds are our project’s own analytical definition, not an official NASA classification.

GlobTraceX presents regional patterns through maps and time-based visualisations, helping users investigate where and when hot-humid conditions occur. The platform is designed to support further comparison and statistical examination of environmental trends.

Why It Matters

Environmental datasets can be difficult to interpret when presented as isolated measurements or technical data tables. GlobTraceX aims to bridge this accessibility gap by connecting geographic exploration with understandable visual evidence.

The platform is intended for students, educators, researchers, and people interested in environmental change. It can encourage data literacy, support evidence-based discussion, and make environmental investigation more approachable.

Creativity and Innovation

Our approach combines a region-based investigation workflow, a clearly defined combined temperature-humidity indicator, interactive geographic presentation, and trend-oriented visual exploration in one platform.

Rather than treating every observation as a standalone number, GlobTraceX encourages users to examine patterns across locations and time. Its focus is on making the process of environmental investigation more transparent, accessible, and understandable.

Development Approach

The project website was developed using an AI-assisted web development workflow and deployed through Vercel. NASA POWER provides the meteorological data source used for the Hot & Humid Days indicator. The team focused on combining data access, geographic presentation, visual communication, and an accessible user experience.

Our design and development decisions prioritise clarity, usability, transparency about indicator definitions, and the responsible presentation of environmental information.

Intended Impact

GlobTraceX aims to help transform complex environmental data into information that more people can explore and understand. By making regional patterns easier to investigate, we hope to encourage curiosity, scientific thinking, and more informed conversations about our changing planet.
